Problem[edit]

A fair die is rolled four times. The probability that each of the final three rolls is at least as large as the roll preceding it may be expressed in the form where and are relatively prime positive integers. Find .

Solution 13 (Pattern recognition)[edit]

If we take the probability for only two rolls, we see that if the first roll is a there is only one number that can come in the next roll. If the first roll is a five then the next roll has two possibilities (5 or 6) and so on. Total of this would be . If we go a step further by analysing the probability for three rolls, we see by bashing that the number of cases are the sum of the first 6 triangular numbers, which is 56. Similarly for four rolls we see that this can be extended by looping this process (sum of sum of triangular numbers) which would give us 126. The probability is therefore . . ~dohnjoe
